speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you're experiencing a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me understand your condition better, have these symptoms appeared all at once or did they develop over a few days?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease (Incompatible with age and viral prodrome; clinical picture of rash, fever, and facial erythema sparing perioral area is more consistent with Scarlet Fever or secondary syphilis, but the specific "sparing perioral area" description with a 1-week prodrome of URI symptoms in an 11-year-old strongly points to a viral exanthem like Enterovirus or a drug reaction. However, the most classic fit for "rash + fever + facial rash sparing nose" is Scarlet Fever. Let's confirm the rash characteristics and medication history.)
